newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Hubco denies breaching accord.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Hubco denies breaching accord.

text.p: Pakistan's state power utility told the country's biggest private power company on Friday that it planned to scrap its power purchase agreement.

Mike Woodroffe, chief executive of Hub Power Co Ltd (Hubco), told Reuters in an interview that he had received a fax from the Water and Power Development Authority (WAPDA) informing him that WAPDA intended to terminate the agreement within 30 days.
WAPDA said it was taking this action because the seal on one of two meters installed at Hubco to measure electricity transmitted to the national grid was broken in March.
Woodroffe said the matter had been under discussion with WAPDA for some time, but claimed WAPDA's action was unjustified.
"We have not committed any fundamental breach of the agreement that could lead to (its) termination," he said.
"Someone or some group is out there to make mischief. I presume it could be part of a campaign launched in the press against private power plants during the past few days," he said.
Newspapers have been casting a critical spotlight on power purchase agreements signed with about two dozen private power companies by the former government led by Benazir Bhutto.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif sparked the debate by setting up a committee last month to review the agreements and seek ways of reducing the tariffs payable to the private power firms.
Woodroffe said he feared that WAPDA's action would hurt Pakistan's reputation, even if the dispute blew over.
"What they do not realise is that I will have to advise the stock exchanges and the foreign bankers over this matter.
"My present concern is that the notice will be regarded as a real potential threat though it has no substance. It will not be appreciated outside Pakistan," he said.
Woodroffe said he planned to approach government officials in Islamabad to try to resolve the matter.
"Earlier we had asked WAPDA to fix the broken seal of the meter but they had not done that, and had termed our explanations evasive and unsatisfactory," he said.
Britain's National Power and Saudi Arabia's Xenel Industries Ltd have major stakes in the World Bank-backed, $1.5-billion, 1,292-megawatt Hubco plant that was completed in February.
Hubco's 10-rupee stock tumbled 0.30 rupee on Friday to close at 37.60 at 6:15 p.m. (1315 GMT) at the Karachi bourse.
